setup.why: Confirm the declared 0-comment baseline on TC-54458 before writing, per task instructions and the sibling's prior sweep finding 0 comments everywhere in the fixture pool.

Re-read storage after the write to verify the comment actually persisted (do not trust the 2xx on the write alone), and to capture the field-by-field shape of a real stored comment for the first time in this suite.

attempts.changed: n/a - first attempt, built exactly as declared: flat body field `comment` (per the json_path-is-not-call-shape lesson, sent flat rather than nested under a `comment` wrapper despite the declared json_path `/comment/comment`), plain text (not HTML), correct integer path params. Succeeded on the first try; no second or third attempt was needed.

notes:
WRITE SUCCEEDED FIRST TRY. Comment id 1307, text '__mcp-probe-comment-2026-09-18T07:36:35Z', posted on TC-54458 (int 1975349, folder 764828, project int 379335744). Re-read confirmed count went 0 -> 1 and the exact same object (id 1307, same text, same created_at 2026-09-18T07:36:43.727Z) is present via get_test_case_comments_v1 -- this write is NOT a false-success like the batch-6 test_run cases; storage genuinely changed.

Field-by-field check of the stored comment against the declared item shape (id/user_id{id,full_name,email}/group_id/project_id/parent_id/entity_id/entity_type/created_at/comment/edited/is_editable/review_status):
- id: present, integer (1307). Matches.
- user_id: present, object with id (2522, int), full_name ('ing'), email ('probe-user@example.invalid'). All three sub-fields present and typed as declared. Matches.
- group_id: present, integer (2615). Matches (this field is in the nested schema but is ABSENT from the flat `returns` array on both add_test_case_comment_v1 and get_test_case_comments_v1 -- confirms the standing 'flat returns array is unreliable' lesson yet again).
- project_id: present, integer (379335744), equals the project id passed in the path. Matches.
- parent_id: present, null. Matches declared 'always null through this path'.
- entity_id: present, integer (1975349) -- **this is exactly the test_case_id from the path**, not 'the id of the run/case mapping cell' as the schema literally describes it. For this capability there is no run/case mapping cell at all: it comments directly on a bare test case. So the entity_id description is DRIFT (copy-pasted from a test-run-comment capability) even though the field itself is present with a plausible-looking integer.
- entity_type: present, value **'TestCase'** -- NOT 'TRTC' as declared (schema literally has `"example": "TRTC"` and the description text 'TRTC for a comment on a test case inside a test run'). This resolves the open question from the task: case comments and run-case comments do NOT share one storage type/enum value here -- add_test_case_comment_v1 / get_test_case_comments_v1 return entity_type 'TestCase' for a genuine bare-test-case comment. The declared 'TRTC' value (and its description) appears to have been copied from a different, run-scoped comment capability and is simply wrong for this one. This is the single most notable finding of this probe.
- created_at: present, ISO datetime string ('2026-09-18T07:36:43.727Z'). Matches.
- comment: present, string, exactly the text sent back verbatim (no HTML wrapping was added since plain text was sent). Matches.
- edited: present, boolean, false (correct, unedited). Matches.
- is_editable: present, boolean, true (correct, author-owned, freshly created). Matches.
- review_status: ABSENT from the response. This matches the schema's own caveat ('present only on comments that were recorded as part of a review verdict') since this comment was not part of a review verdict -- correctly absent, not treated as declared_missing.

No undeclared fields were returned beyond the declared comment-object properties.

Also re-confirms the standing json_path lesson: the declared json_path for the body field is '/comment/comment' (implying a nested wrapper {comment:{comment:...}}), but the working call used a flat body {comment:'...'} directly, exactly as the capability's own schema note says ('the published spec wraps it under an extra `comment` key that the server does not send') -- so in this rare case the capability's own guidance already flags the json_path as misleading, and the flat call was correct and worked on the first attempt.

Severity: the entity_type/entity_id description drift is functional/documentation-level (moderate) -- a caller relying on entity_type=='TRTC' to detect a case-level comment, or relying on the entity_id description to look up a run/case mapping row, would be wrong. The write itself is fully reliable (no false success). This comment is permanent residue (deletes are refused as destructive) -- id 1307 on TC-54458, text '__mcp-probe-comment-2026-09-18T07:36:35Z', is the first and only comment in this fixture pool as of this probe.
